そば家鶴小（ちるぐゎー）.name: Soba-ya Chiruguwa
そば家鶴小（ちるぐゎー）.desc: The Chatan branch of Chiruguwa, an old-folk-house-style shop with a beautiful red-tiled roof. Its unusual beef soba is a bowl where the savory flavor of stir-fried beef and vegetables blends into the pork bone broth. Even the tissue holder doubles as a menu, which is a charming touch. It's also close to American Village.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 4 Sonnet) and partly edited by me lol 🍜✨

I ate here in December 2024 😄 This time I was exploring roads I don't usually take, hoping to discover a new Okinawa soba shop, and I found this place in Chatan, Chatan Town! It's "Soba-ya Chiruguwa Chatan Branch," with a beautiful exterior topped by a classic Okinawan red-tiled roof ✨
Soba-ya Chiruguwa
Soba-ya Chiruguwa

When you step inside, the interior is styled like an old Okinawan folk house, with a very calm atmosphere. On the tables are menus with Okinawan-style patterns, and just looking at them gets me excited 🎵
Inside the shop

What I ordered this time was the "Beef Soba"! A beef dish is rare at an Okinawa soba shop, and it reminded me of the beef soba at Maeda Shokudo. My expectations rose as I wondered what it would taste like 🤤
Beef soba ¥990
First, I start with the broth. The pork-bone-based broth is mixed with the juices from the stir-fried beef and vegetables. It's a broth with a flavor a little different from regular Okinawa soba 😋
Beef soba ¥990
Next, the noodles. They're thin, straight noodles with a very soft texture 👍

And now the star of the show, the stir-fried beef and vegetables! The generous heap of beef and vegetables looks very voluminous and filling. The beef is simmered until tender, and the vegetables keep their crunch while soaking up plenty of flavor 🥬

When you eat the beef, vegetables, and noodles together, the savory flavors of each ingredient harmonize in your mouth, making it a very satisfying bowl. It's not as big as the beef soba at Maeda Shokudo, but it's still enough to fill you up 😊

Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. This shop is located in Chatan Town, close to American Village, so it's a convenient place to drop by between sightseeing stops. Being able to enjoy beef soba while soaking up the atmosphere of an Okinawan old folk house is a real draw 🏠 If you want to enjoy Okinawa soba in the Chatan area, I'd definitely like you to give this shop a try 😄

そば専門 てだこ.name: Soba Senmon Tedako
そば専門 てだこ.desc: A popular Urasoe shop marked by its red-tiled roof. The balance between the creamy pork bone broth and the chewy homemade flat noodles is excellent, approaching the level of my recommended shops. The menu is wide-ranging too, with natto soba and chilled dishes.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions by me.
This time I'd like to introduce "Soba Senmon Tedako" in Nakama, Urasoe. I made a new discovery on my Okinawa soba tour!
Soba specialty shop Tedako
First of all, the shop's exterior made an impression. The red-tiled roof and the "Tedako" sign catch your eye. It's full of Okinawan atmosphere 😍

When I went inside, since it was lunchtime, it was bustling with locals and tourists. You can really feel the vibe of a popular shop 🎵 Being lively is proof of a good shop. (This time there were so many customers inside that I couldn't take photos of the interior, sorry 🙏)
Menu (natto soba (^0^;) I'd never seen that before)
Menu
Menu (plenty of chilled dishes too)
Menu
From the menu I decided to order the standard "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba" 😋
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba, medium ¥800
Now, here comes the long-awaited "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba"!
First I tasted the broth. The pork-bone-based broth is very creamy with a smooth mouthfeel. Pretty tasty, a high level 😊
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba, medium ¥800

Next I tried the noodles. I heard Tedako's noodles are homemade flat noodles. Their chewy texture is distinctive, and they cling well to the broth. They go down smoothly too, and I just kept eating and eating.

And then the main topping, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They're simmered until meltingly tender, soft enough to pull apart with chopsticks. However, I can't say they were perfect; I felt a few slightly stringy parts.

Overall, I felt that Soba Senmon Tedako's "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba" is a bowl at a level that doesn't fall short of my recommended shops. The balance between the broth and noodles is especially exquisite, and it's packed with the appeal of Okinawa soba.
I'm curious about the other menu items too. The "Spicy Mazesoba" and "Yomogi (Mugwort) Soba" looked delicious. Next time I'd like to try a different dish 😆

Rating (10/15): All things considered, I'd say Soba Senmon Tedako is close to the level of my recommended shops. The broth and noodles in particular are excellent, and I think it's an irresistible bowl for Okinawa soba lovers. The location is convenient too, so please stop by when you visit Urasoe. You can enjoy authentic Okinawa soba in a lively atmosphere, mingling with the locals. Okinawa soba lovers, Soba Senmon Tedako is a shop you should check out! Next time, please visit it yourselves. I'm sure you'll discover a new side of Okinawa soba's appeal 😉

そば屋よしこ.name: Sobaya Yoshiko
そば屋よしこ.desc: A long-established shop with a yellow sign standing at the gateway to Soba Road (Prefectural Route 84). Featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app, its specialty is a hearty pig's feet soba with three big pieces of pig's feet (tebichi) topped with lettuce.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and partly edited by me lol 🍜✨

I ate here in November 2024 😄 This time I'd like to introduce "Sobaya Yoshiko" in Izumi, Motobu Town. This shop was featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app, and it's a place I'd been curious about for a while 🔍
It's featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app 😆
Sobaya Yoshiko
Sobaya Yoshiko
Shop entrance

Located along Prefectural Route 84, this is a long-established soba shop that has been loved by locals for many years. Its bright yellow sign is the landmark, and the noren (shop curtain) reading "Yoshiko Soba" flutters in the wind 🏮
Inside, there's an old-fashioned atmosphere, and many photos and autographs were posted on the walls. It was bustling with local customers and tourists, and lots of people came in that day too 😄
Inside the shop
Looking at the menu, it lists classic dishes like soki soba, pig's feet (tebichi) soba, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba. The menu has photos, so it's easy to understand 👍
Menu
Menu
This time I ordered the "Pig's Feet Soba" that was featured on Horiemon's Teriyaki app. Tebichi means pig's feet; it's packed with collagen and is a popular topping among women too 🐷

After waiting a while, the "Pig's Feet Soba" was brought out. First, the visual impact! Like "Oshiro Soba" in Okita, Nago, which I introduce among my "Okinawa soba shops that don't fall short of my recommended shops," it's distinctive for being topped with lettuce 🥬
Pig's feet (tebichi) soba, large ¥850
As always, I start by tasting the broth. This shop's broth is a blended stock of pork bone, bonito, and kelp, with a gentle flavor where the bonito comes through a bit 😋
Pig's feet (tebichi) soba, large ¥850
Next, the noodles. The medium-thick, straight, softish noodles cling well to the broth and are decently tasty 🍜

And as for the pig's feet (tebichi) topping, there are three big pieces, making it very voluminous! They're slowly simmered, so the meat is meltingly soft and tender. Packed with collagen, it seems good for your skin too ✨
After finishing, I was left with a warm feeling of nostalgia. It was a bowl that made me understand why it's been loved for so long by locals and tourists alike 😌

By the way, on Horiemon's Teriyaki app this shop's pig's feet soba is introduced as a recommendation, and it is decently tasty, but I thought the pig's feet soba at "Nanbu Soba" in Shiozaki, Itoman, was tastier than this one 🎵
Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. It's a shop popular with locals and tourists, so why not stop by when you head toward Motobu Town? 😊

そば＆酒膳処一本松.name: Soba & Shuzen-dokoro Ipponmatsu
そば＆酒膳処一本松.desc: An izakaya at night that serves Okinawa soba lunches during the day. It's a treasure trove of unusual dishes like taco soba, tomato sauce soba, and tropical soba, and its signature is the soupless dandan-noodle-style "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba." The chewy fresh noodles are delicious.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (Oct 1, 2023 to Feb 29, 2024)," and I went here as my 12th of 34 shops 😊
Soba & Shuzen-dokoro Ipponmatsu. I thought it was just an izakaya (;^ω^)
I'd thought this shop was an ordinary izakaya, but thanks to this stamp rally I learned for the first time that they do Okinawa soba lunches at midday (;^ω^)
The interior does feel like an izakaya, but this time I decided to order the "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba" that was featured in the stamp rally booklet.
This dish was also featured at the very beginning of the menu. Is it their top pick, I wonder?
It was featured at the very beginning of the menu: "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba"
After ordering, as I flipped through the menu, I noticed that Ipponmatsu has quite an array of unusual Okinawa soba dishes 😁
This is "Tomato Sauce Soba," which I think was developed for the Okinawa soba stamp rally two years ago. I'm curious what it tastes like lol
A pasta-style (vongole?) Okinawa soba, and a pork-and-egg Okinawa soba lol. Quirky.
The pig's feet (tebichi) soba is normal, but the menu photo above is apparently "Taco Soba." I wonder what that's like (;^ω^)
Vegetable soba and squid ink soba. These are normal.
Dandan noodle soba and pork bone soba. These are fairly normal too.
Mapo tofu soba: this one looks soupier than what I ordered. "Braised Pork Belly Cheese Soba": this one's quirky too 😊
Curry soba and pork offal (nakami) soba. These are pretty common.
"Kake Soba" and "Grated Yam Soba." Unusual ones 🤗
Apparently this is "Tropical Soba." It seems to be topped with pineapple too (;^ω^)
While I was enjoying looking at all the quirky dishes, the "Okinawan-Style Mapo Soba" I ordered arrived.
Okinawan-style mapo soba ¥950
Usually I'd taste the broth, but this Okinawa soba is like soupless dandan noodles; instead of broth, it's mapo tofu sitting on top of Okinawa soba noodles.
So I decided to eat it by mixing the mapo tofu with the noodles 😊

The noodles seem to be fresh noodles, with a chewy texture, and they're delicious 😋 I'd imagined the mapo tofu would be a bit spicy, but it's not spicy at all; this is a flavor even kids would have no problem with 😁
The crunchy texture of the onions is a nice accent.

Rating (9.5/15): It was an Okinawa soba like a mapo tofu version of soupless dandan noodles 😊 The fresh noodles had a chewy texture and were delicious. Since it's mapo tofu, personally I'd have liked it a bit spicy.

たこ焼きちゃんぽん.name: Takoyaki Champon
たこ焼きちゃんぽん.desc: A shop with outstanding value for money in the characterful Chuo Ichibangai area of Okinawa City. Vegetable soba at an astonishing ¥400, with a gentle pork bone broth and plenty of vegetables. A welcome find in this era of rising prices.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😄
Takoyaki Champon (it's across from Densuke Shoten in Chuo Ichibangai, Okinawa City 😆)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)
Menu posted inside the shop (cheap, right 😄)

This is the menu posted inside the shop, and everything is at reasonable prices you won't find at other shops 😄 With so many products and shops raising prices due to soaring costs and wage increases, can they really make a profit at these prices? Maybe they have another source of income lol
From the menu I decided to order the super-reasonable "Vegetable Soba." ¥400, so cheap 😄
Vegetable soba ¥400
The vegetable soba arrived. It has a decent amount of volume 😄 First I taste the broth.
It's a gentle broth with a bit of a pork bone base coming through. Decently tasty.
Vegetable soba ¥400

The noodles are medium-thick, straight, and soft. For toppings, egg and pork luncheon meat (Spam) are cut into thin strips and added as accents. There's quite a lot of vegetables, and the seasoning is on the light side. I'm always eating Okinawa soba that's nothing but carbs and meat, so getting some vegetables in seems to make my nutritional balance a little better 😆
Rating (9/15): A great-value Okinawa soba in the characterful Chuo Ichibangai area of Okinawa City. The taste is decently good too, so why not give it a try at least once 😄

Its pride is the soft-bone soba in a rich, hearty broth with plenty of bonito flavor, a deep taste only an izakaya could create, a bit different from the first shop. Relax in its tatami-seating style.

I ate here in January 2025 😄 This time I visited "Daruma Soba" in Sobe, Yomitan Village. Actually, this shop is the second branch of "Daruma Soba" in Yamazato, Okinawa City. It's combined with an izakaya called "Sumiya," so I headed right over to see what kind of Okinawa soba they serve! 😄
Daruma Soba
Daruma Soba (shop entrance)
By the way, this is "Daruma Soba" in Yamazato, Okinawa City (the daruma logos really do look alike 😆)

The interior has a warm, wood-based design, and it's a tatami-seating style where you take off your shoes and step up. 🏮 It has a casual izakaya-like feel, and its charm is that you can enjoy Okinawa soba while relaxing at your leisure.

The menu is extensive, so you can enjoy not just Okinawa soba but also lunch sets and all kinds of Okinawan dishes. Okinawa soba made by an izakaya, so my expectations rose a bit! ✨
This time, from the menu, I ordered the "Soft-Bone Soba (Medium)."
Soft-bone soba, medium ¥800

The broth has a rich flavor with plenty of bonito broth coming through. As you'd expect from an izakaya making it, you can really taste the depth. Its defining feature is a rich broth for which the word "hearty" is a perfect fit. It's a little different from the broth at a typical Okinawa soba shop; if anything, it's a somewhat distinctive flavor that feels packed with the izakaya's particular care. Maybe this is the reason the taste differs between the second and first shops.
Soft-bone soba, medium ¥800
The noodles are medium-thick wavy noodles, but they have a surprisingly soft texture 🍝

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) 🍖 are well seasoned through and have a tender texture. However, they're not completely fall-apart tender; a bit of sinewy texture remains. The broth also has an oily quality, so I think it'll be irresistible for people who like rich, hearty flavors 🎉

Rating (10.5/15): Looking at it overall, I really feel this shop serves Okinawa soba with a good balance of noodles, broth, and toppings. They say it tastes different from the first shop in Yamazato, Okinawa City, and personally I found this second branch in Sobe, Yomitan Village, tastier. It's a bowl I can truly recommend to anyone who likes hearty flavors. Its unique depth and richness are something only an izakaya could deliver. If you ever head toward Yomitan Village, please do stop by at least once 😋
